evidence: GroupPermissionEvaluator.java canManage() Javadoc says 'For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups', which documents the bug in GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). canManage() backs requireManage(), which GroupsResource.java:181 (addTopLevelGroup) uses, so VIEW should not be enough. Fix the implementation to MANAGE only and update the Javadoc to match.

GroupPermissionEvaluator.java: the requireManageMembers() Javadoc says it throws if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} is false, but GroupPermissions.java:376-380 actually calls canManageMembers(group). So the Javadoc is wrong. The reviewer got the details backwards: it doesn't point at canManage(), and the correct target is canManageMembers(GroupModel), not canManageMembership(GroupModel).
GroupPermissionEvaluator.java getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() Javadoc says '@return Stream of IDs...' but the method signature returns Set<String>. This is a documentation-only fix.

GroupPermissionsV2.java:65-71: canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). Because hasPermission (lines 156-162) returns true if ANY listed scope is granted, an all-groups VIEW-only permission passes requireManage() and lets the admin create top-level groups (GroupsResource.java:181). canManage(GroupModel) at line 79 correctly checks MANAGE only. Should be hasPermission(null, MANAGE).

GroupPermissionsV2.java:121-124 passes groupResource.getId() (authz resource UUID) to hasPermission and adds it to the result. hasPermission (line 141) looks resources up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), and AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource names per-group resources after the group ID (resolveGroup returns group.getId()). So findByName misses and falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned IDs are resource IDs. UsersResource.java:448-450 then puts them in UserModel.GROUPS as group IDs, so they never match. V1 (GroupPermissions.java:315) uses resource.getName() correctly. Should use groupResource.getName().

RolePermissions.java:302: before the PR the line was 'if (root.users().canManageDefault()) return checkAdminRoles(role);'. The removed UserPermissions.canManageDefault() was exactly root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS), so the new line behaves the same and no shortcut was removed. Returning true immediately would skip checkAdminRoles(role), which stops a manage-users admin from mapping admin roles they don't hold. That would be a privilege escalation.

MgmtPermissions.java:163-174: hasOneAdminRole only checks client roles of the realm-management or master '<realm>-realm' client (identity.hasOneClientRole). AdminRoles.ADMIN ('admin') is a master realm role, not one of those client roles, so it was a dead check there. Master 'admin' and realm-management 'realm-admin' are composites that include manage-users/view-users, so those admins still hit the MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS fast path. V1 UserPermissions.canView/canManage never checked ADMIN either.

AdminPermissions.java:73-99: the refactor only moves the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check from inside onEvent() to around registration. Feature flags are static, so behavior is unchanged: V2-only deployments never got this cleanup before the PR either. The lack of V2 resource cleanup on group/client/role removal is a real but pre-existing gap. The suggested fix is also wrong: in V2 the listener would call GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (GroupPermissionsV2.java:173), which throws UnsupportedOperationException. V2 cleanup needs its own mechanism.

test-framework ApiUtil.java:9-14: response.getLocation().getPath() would NPE if the Location header were missing. This is test-only code, and the same dereference was there before the PR. An NPE still fails the test, so an assertNotNull only gives a clearer failure message. It fixes no bug.

RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:34-36 adds QUERY_GROUPS to 'myadmin'. The fixture is shared through AbstractPermissionTest by UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest and GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest. GroupPermissions.java:148-150 canList() returns true on QUERY_GROUPS before evaluating V2 permissions, so no test can exercise the permission-based list path. No current test asserts that path, so nothing is broken today. It is a test coverage/design concern.
